title: Imperial Science Cafe: Targeting Metabolism to Treat Cancer
desc:
Join us for the next Imperial Science Cafe: Targeting Metabolism to Treat Cancer at Maggie’s West London .

Cancer cells behave differently from healthy cells, including the way they use and process nutrients. This session will explore how researchers are learning to “starve” cancer by targeting its altered metabolism. We will explain how cancer cells use metabolic fuels in unique ways, and how these differences can be turned into treatment opportunities. Attendees will hear how scientists are developing drugs that block key metabolic pathways, aiming to slow tumour growth while sparing normal tissues. We will also discuss how diet, the immune system, and existing therapies like chemotherapy might interact with cancer metabolism. The session will highlight promising clinical trials,…

title: IDE Seminar Series – Prof Steven Riley
desc:
Public health dynamics for respiratory virus outbreaks and pandemics

Respiratory viruses pose a significant and recurring health security risk. From SARS1, through pandemic influenza and COVID-19, infectious disease dynamics has helped inform our response. In this talk, I’ll discuss some key questions and answers from historical outbreaks before thinking about how a future pandemic might unfold. I’ll also discuss how these topics relate to the recently published UK Pandemic Preparedness Plan.

Location: White City, School of Public Health Building Room: SPH 204 – Seminar Room I n-person event. If you wish to join online, please register here.
venue: SPH 204 - Seminar Room , School of Public Health, White City Campus
